cards.front: Recall a key point about Resource Allocation
cards.back: A market is any opportunity for buyers and sellers to interact to establish price — physical or virtual.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Resource Allocation
cards.back: Factor markets trade factors of production (labour market, capital market). Product markets trade finished goods and services to consumers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Resource Allocation
cards.back: The price mechanism allocates resources: rising prices signal shortage, attracting producers; falling prices signal surplus, driving producers away. Functions: signalling, rationing, incentivising.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Resource Allocation
cards.back: Primary sector extracts raw materials (farming). Secondary manufactures goods (factories). Tertiary provides services (retail, finance). The UK is ~80% tertiary.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Resource Allocation
cards.back: Deindustrialisation is the decline of secondary sector employment in developed economies due to globalisation, automation, and rising demand for services.

cards.front: What should you know about economics exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating resource allocation, use the SRI framework: Signalling (do prices reflect scarcity?), Rationing (are goods allocated to those who value them most?), Incentivising (do prices encourage efficient production?).
Prices signal scarcity/surplus (e.g. Policy announcements signal priorities)
Profit motivates producers (e.g. Subsidies/taxes change behaviour)
High prices limit demand (e.g. Queuing, eligibility criteria, vouchers)
Generally efficient but can fail (e.g. Can correct failure but may cause new issues)
Allocates to those who can pay (e.g. Can prioritise need over ability to pay)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: The price mechanism always allocates resources fairly. Correct: The price mechanism allocates efficiently (to those willing to pay), but not fairly. It rations goods to those with purchasing power, meaning the poor may be unable to afford essentials. This is why governments intervene with subsidies, welfare, and free public services.
Evaluate whether the price mechanism is the best way to allocate resources in an economy.
AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Resource Allocation with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

cards.front: How the Price Mechanism Allocates Resources
cards.back: In a free market economy, resources are allocated through the price mechanism — the system by which prices, set by the forces of demand and supply, signal to producers and consumers what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce.
